transcript.content: Hello. I am a board-certified psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm having a really hard time remembering what happened during a terrible event two weeks ago. Parts of it are just completely blank, and ever since, I've been feeling extremely on edge and unable to relax. It's been like this every day for the past two weeks and I'm just so exhausted.
To help me understand what you are experiencing, could you tell me a little more about the terrible event that occurred two weeks ago?

I really struggle to talk about it because my memory of that day is so patchy and fragmented. The majority of what happened is just a complete blank to me, so I can't really explain the details of what occurred. I only remember random, disconnected pieces.
I understand it is difficult to recall. Even if the details are blurry, did this event involve a threat to your life, physical safety, or the safety of someone else?

I understand why you're asking, but my memory of that day is just too blurry and fragmented. Because of these blank spots, I honestly can't recall the specific details of what happened or whether there was a direct threat to my life or safety. It is all just a complete fog right now.
Even though your memory of the event is blurry, do you find yourself experiencing any sudden, unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks related to it?

No, I don't really experience sudden flashbacks, unwanted memories, or nightmares about the event. My main issue is actually the opposite, where I just can't remember large parts of what happened. It is mostly just a big blank space in my mind.
Since that event, have you been actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, or conversations about it, or avoiding people, places, or situations that might remind you of it?
I haven't really noticed myself avoiding those things, to be honest. Since I can't remember most of what happened anyway, I'm not really sure if I've been actively avoiding reminders of it.
Since the event, have you had any trouble falling or staying asleep, or have you found it difficult to concentrate on daily tasks?
I haven't really had major issues with sleeping or concentrating. I'm not quite sure about those specific symptoms, as nothing stands out to me in those areas.
Since the event, have you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, as if you are in a dream or things around you are unreal?
No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. I don't feel detached from myself, and my surroundings still seem completely real to me.
Since the event, have you found it difficult to experience positive emotions, such as happiness, love, or satisfaction?
I haven't really noticed any change in my ability to feel positive emotions. I still feel love and happiness just like before, so I don't think that is an issue for me.
Have these feelings of being on edge and the gaps in your memory caused significant difficulties in your work, social life, or other important areas of your daily routine?
I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about how these issues are affecting my work or social life yet. I've just been focused on trying to get through each day.
Prior to this event two weeks ago, have you ever experienced similar episodes of memory loss or felt this level of anxiety, or is this completely new for you?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before. These memory issues and this constant anxiety are completely new to me, and they only started after the event two weeks ago.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports significant anxiety, feeling on edge, and localized amnesia starting immediately after a stressful event two weeks ago. While these symptoms are trauma-related, they do not meet the minimum symptom threshold (9 or more symptoms) required for a diagnosis of Acute Stress Disorder, nor do they meet the one-month duration requirement for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, making Adjustment Disorder the most appropriate diagnosis.
